intro: The Hebrew alphabet with the sound of every letter, how to find the vowels in unpointed text, the main reading rules, and a key to the symbols in the pronunciations.

sections.heading: How the Hebrew alphabet works
text: Hebrew is written from right to left in an alphabet of 22 letters, all consonants. There are no capital letters, but five letters take a different shape at the end of a word: ך ם ן ף ץ.

Vowels can be shown with dots and dashes (niqqud), but everyday Hebrew leaves them out — on signs, in books, on phones. This app writes words the way you will see them, and the pronunciation under each word gives the vowels.

items.note: alef: a light catch in the throat, or silent; often just carries a vowel
bet / vet: b at the start of a word, often v in the middle or at the end
gimel: hard g; ג׳ with a geresh is j, as in "jam"
dalet
he: h; silent at the end of a word (שנה [ʃaˈna])
vav: v, or the vowel o or u; doubled וו is v in the middle of a word
zayin; ז׳ is the s in "measure"
chet: kh, as in "loch"
tet
yod: y, or the vowel i; doubled יי is y in the middle of a word
kaf / khaf: k at the start of a word, often kh elsewhere; ך at the end of a word is always kh
lamed
mem; ם at the end of a word
nun; ן at the end of a word
samekh
ayin: in standard Israeli speech the same as alef
pe / fe: p at the start of a word, often f elsewhere; ף at the end of a word is f
tsadi: ts; ץ at the end of a word; צ׳ is ch, as in "chips"
qof: the same as כ said as k
resh: r at the back of the throat, as in French
shin / sin: usually sh, sometimes s
tav: the same as ט

sections.heading: Full spelling: finding the vowels
text: Without niqqud, Hebrew uses "full spelling" (ktiv male), the official rules for unpointed text. Some vowels are shown by adding a letter:
ו stands for o or u: שולחן [ʃulˈχan] table, אוכל [ˈoχel] food. י stands for i (and sometimes e): תיק [tik] bag, עיפרון [ipaˈʁon] pencil.
Because ו and י can be vowels, a consonant v or y in the middle of a word is written double: אוויר [aˈviʁ] air, עגבנייה [aɡvaniˈja] tomato.
a and e are usually not written at all: ספר [ˈsefeʁ] book. At the end of a word they are often shown with ה or א: שנה [ʃaˈna] year, אמא [ˈima] mom.
Some words still have to be learned whole — the same letters can spell different words, and context tells you which.

sections.heading: Reading rules
text: Stress usually falls on the last syllable, but many common words stress the one before it (ספר [ˈsefeʁ], בית [ˈbajit]). The IPA in this app always marks it with ˈ.
Several short words are written joined to the word after them: ו "and", ה "the", ב "in", ל "to", מ "from", ש "that", כש "when". So בבית is "in the house" and ושלום is "and hello".
In standard Israeli speech ח and כ sound the same (kh), as do ט and ת, כ and ק, and א and ע. The distinctions survive only in spelling.

sections.heading: Symbols used in the pronunciations
sections.text: Each symbol that doesn't sound the way an English speaker might expect, with a word from the vocabulary that uses it.

items.note: open a, as in "father" but shorter
pure e, like "ay" in "say" without the glide
ee, as in "machine"
pure o, like "oh" without the glide
oo, as in "food"
y, as in "yes"
r made at the back of the throat (French r)
sh, as in "ship"
s, as in "measure"
a catch in the throat, as in "uh-oh"
always a hard g, as in "go"
the next syllable is stressed
kh, as in Scottish "loch" (Hebrew ח and כ)
